title: Separate two charges
hook: Change separation and predict electric-force magnitude.
misconception: electric-force magnitude doubles when separation doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply F = kabs(q₁q₂)/r² to compare electric-force magnitude when separation changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With two fixed point charges in the same medium, F = kabs(q₁q₂)/r². When separation doubles, electric-force magnitude becomes ¼ times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model F = kabs(q₁q₂)/r²; scaling exponent -2. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider two fixed point charges in the same medium, with a nonzero initial result. If separation triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on electric-force magnitude?
recall.why: Apply F = kabs(q₁q₂)/r² under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/9.
